key_insight: A two-stage RL congestion-management pipeline—violation pre-classification plus actor-critic control—can robustly curtail low-voltage grid overloads even with sparse observability and noisy measurements.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical control strategy for PV-rich, EV-charging, and heat-pump-heavy distribution grids where curative actions must remain effective despite imperfect sensing and model uncertainty.
method: Random-forest pre-classifier detects likely grid-limit violations.
Actor-critic controller decides curtailment actions after detection.
Robustness is tested against measurement noise and grid-parameter mismatch in a real low-voltage grid scenario.
evidence_signal: On a real low-voltage grid with synthetic future scenarios, the approach reduced total violation magnitude by 98.9% with accurate grid parameters and stayed nearly unchanged under the tested noise levels.
watch_item: Performance becomes more sensitive under grid-model mismatch, so deployment will need careful parameter validation and adaptation.
paper_title: Robustness of Reinforcement Learning-Based Congestion Management in Low-Voltage Grids
